title: Categorical Data: Mode, Relative Frequency and Percent Bar Graphs
seo_title: Grade 6 Categorical Data and Relative Frequency Worksheets: Percent Bar Graphs (TEKS 6.12D, STAAR)
standard_text: 6.12D summarize categorical data with numerical and graphical summaries, including the mode, the percent of values in each category (relative frequency table), and the percent bar graph, and use these summaries to describe the data distribution
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 worksheets for Texas TEKS 6.12D: the mode of categorical data, relative frequency tables, percents of categories, percent bar graphs and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: 9 of 30 = 0.3 = 30%. All the relative frequencies add to 100%.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Categorical data are names or labels, such as favorite sport. You cannot find a mean, but you can find the mode.
  • Relative frequency = frequency ÷ total. It can be a fraction, decimal or percent: 6 of 24 = 1/4 = 0.25 = 25%.
  • The relative frequencies of all the categories add to 1 (or 100%).
  • A percent bar graph shows each category as part of one bar that equals 100%.

Examples

Example

Soccer: 9 of 30 students

9 ÷ 30 = 0.3

Answer: 30%

Example

Bar: Bus 45%. 80 students surveyed.

0.45 × 80

Answer: 36 students

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using the count as the relative frequencyDivide the count by the total.
Dividing by the wrong totalThe total is the sum of all the frequencies.
Reading a percent bar as countsThe bar shows percents; multiply by the total to get counts.

faq.a: Summarize categorical data with numerical and graphical summaries, including the mode, the percent of values in each category (relative frequency table) and the percent bar graph, and use these summaries to describe the data distribution.

faq.q: Can categorical data have a mean?
faq.a: No. You cannot add labels, so use the mode or relative frequencies.

faq.q: Do relative frequencies always add to 1?
faq.a: Yes. All the parts together make the whole survey.

faq.q: What is a percent bar graph?
faq.a: One bar that stands for 100%, divided into parts for each category.
